leftEvidence.title: Solomon names the promise fulfilled and still asks for it

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Solomon blesses Israel, recounts God’s choice of David and Jerusalem, says he has built what David desired, and asks that the throne word be confirmed.
points.right: Foreign wives turn Solomon toward other gods; the LORD is angry and announces a torn kingdom while preserving one tribe for David and Jerusalem.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places fulfilled building and continuing throne promise remain distinct inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places David becomes a remembered standard and reason inside Solomon’s judgment inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Kings 8:12–26 and 1 Kings 11:1–13 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Solomon’s divided heart is measured against David

payload.tension: 1 Kings 8:12–26 foregrounds fulfilled building and continuing throne promise remain distinct; 1 Kings 11:1–13 foregrounds David becomes a remembered standard and reason inside Solomon’s judgment. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
